ideas.thesis: Core is VOO 70.4% (target 70-80%), satellite QQQ 17.8%, cash 11.8%. Moving ~$8 of idle cash into the core lifts it to ~76% and keeps an ~$8 buffer.

Semis fell -3.4% (SOX) after +80% YTD on the OpenAI revenue reset and the AVGO financing story. SMH is still +5.3% vs 50d and fundamentals look strong (AVGO 10-Q revenue +85% y/y). Add a small semis satellite only if SMH holds its 50d (~$577) into CPI on Oct 14.

ideas.whyRejected: At 17.8% the satellite is within its 30% cap and the 15-20% target; one rotation day (QQQ -1.4%, RSP +0.4%) is not a thesis change.
Overlaps QQQ heavily and RSI 67.6 makes it extended; it adds no diversification.

decision.summary: Top up the VOO core by about $8 at the open, hold QQQ, and put SMH on watch for a satellite add after CPI (Oct 14) if it holds its 50-day.
decision.reasoning: CoreSat sizes by structure first, then uses the satellite for tech/semis upside. Today the structure says top up the core (70% of NAV, bottom of its 70-80% band). The tempting move is buying the semis dip, but the drop came from a demand-narrative shock plus debt-funded capex at 5%+ rates, and the stocks and yields inverse correlation is strong right now. One red day after +80% YTD is not a setup. The rule is to wait for SMH to hold its 50-day through CPI, then add at most ~5% of NAV.

plan.trigger: Unless SPY gaps down >1.5% at the open (then defer to midday)
Not today: re-evaluate after Oct 14 CPI if SMH > 50d SMA

risks: The core is a cap-weighted S&P, so it carries the same AI concentration as the satellite.
A hot CPI on Oct 14 plus a December hike could reprice long-duration tech.
SEC Section 31 fee applies to any satellite trims; TAF is $0 through Dec 31.
